brief.headline: The Hedge Fund De-Gross Is an Entry Point Only for Allocators Buying Diversification
bullets: Hedge Funds: Managers spent the week cutting risk, and some of the largest allocators spent it adding to hedge funds.

brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,561.67 (down 0.4% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 18.7, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.10% (up 12 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.27 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.20%, near long-run norms (down 10 bps on the prior reading).

items.title: BoE’s Bailey: “Interconnectedness” could see private credit pose risk to financial stability
items.takeaway: Private credit may pose a financial stability risk if growing “interconnectedness” means it becomes “one domino in a chain reaction”, according to Andrew Bailey, speaking in his capacity as chair of the Financial Stability Board (FSB).
items.whyItMatters: Private credit has grown into one of the fastest-growing corners of finance as non-bank lenders take share from banks.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.20%, near long-run norms (down 10 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Nov 13.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.
